metadata.evaluation_kind: Independent candidate-only forward-test; pilot paired comparison, not broad certification
metadata.evidence_interpretation: Case evidence paths are relative to candidate_root. Contract JSON reads selected member signatures/docs; initial reference.py calls also displayed raw type trees. Briefs and retained receipt are reference evidence, not new verification. The receipt summary was read; probe sources were not read or rerun. Code sketches omit imports/context and remain uncompiled.
metadata.shared_receipt_scope: Existing receipt reports 13 named assertion tests; no process-RSS, network-I/O or broad-performance certification. Case claims use corresponding decision-brief scopes, not test-name inference alone.

measurement.count_basis: Manually counted issued tool calls through this final artifact validation, including unsuccessful reads.
measurement.output_context_tokens_reason: No end-to-end token/context meter was used; one search output was truncated, and tool pre-truncation estimates do not measure consumed context.
measurement.case_word_count_method: Whitespace-separated string-value words across each case, excluding id, evidence paths and this numeric count; includes API names and Rust sketches.
measurement.artifact_validation: 24 ordered task IDs matched; every cited case evidence path exists; maximum 152 whitespace words per case; JSON reparsed. No Rust compilation or execution.

observed_gaps.detail: TableProviderFilterPushDown::Exact docs say the provider will omit only tuples which pass the filter, contradicting the TableProvider::scan TRUE-row contract. The brief and full scan docs support the chosen Exact behavior.
No retained evidence establishes filter-reuse break-even, production RSS bounds, spill performance or cloud I/O reduction; these remain task-specific measurements.
The brief identifies the Inexact fixture as retaining all candidates; it does not validate a min/max pruning algorithm.
The consulted corpus routes durable data to IPC/Parquet, but no executed cross-version IPC or exact original dictionary-assignment roundtrip was consulted.

retrieval_notes: An initial listing guessed content/decisions, while the route file correctly pointed to content/capabilities.

Three defining-path guesses for RowSelector, ListingOptions and ListingTableConfig were absent; operation-index lookup resolved each. These were evaluator navigation mistakes, not evidence that the APIs were missing.
One broad index search output was truncated; all subsequently relied-on members were retrieved directly.

cases.decision: Use filter_record_batch for one batch; reusable preparation is optional for repeated masks.
cases.decisive_conditions: The Boolean mask addresses the same row domain as the batch.
cases.contract: Input: RecordBatch and nullable BooleanArray. Output: Result<RecordBatch, ArrowError>, containing true-mask rows in source order; false/null mask positions disappear. Existing selected value nulls and duplicates remain. The batch path preserves schema and the tested field/schema metadata. Zero selected rows remain a valid batch; zero-column batches retain selected row count.
cases.implementation_sketch: let out = filter_record_batch(&batch, &mask)?;
cases.unknowns: Nested/extension metadata propagation beyond the documented/tested path is unqualified; enforce intended mask-domain alignment.

cases.decision: Use checked take per column, then reconstruct with fields permitting introduced nulls; the batch helper is convenient after explicit validation.
cases.decisive_conditions: Gather semantics require requested order and duplicates, unlike filtering. take_record_batch exposes no bounds option.
cases.contract: Indices [2,0,2,null] produce four rows: row2,row0,row2,all-null. Null input values also survive. Some(TakeOptions { check_bounds:true }) returns bounds errors; unchecked out-of-range indices may panic. Index-to-usize failure errors. Original non-nullable fields may reject null-index results: preserve metadata while adjusting nullability. For zero columns, supply explicit output row_count.
cases.implementation_sketch:
let cols = batch.columns().iter().map(|a| take(a.as_ref(), &indices, Some(TakeOptions { check_bounds: true }))).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
let out = RecordBatch::try_new(nullable_schema, cols)?;
cases.unknowns: All datatype combinations and nested nullability are not qualified.

cases.decision: Prepare one FilterPredicate and reuse it across the 20 arrays; compare optimized and direct variants before asserting a speedup.
cases.decisive_conditions: Arrays must share the mask row domain. Repeated preparation savings must outweigh optimize time and additional memory.
cases.contract: A borrowed BooleanArray builds an owned predicate representation; filter returns Result<ArrayRef, ArrowError> for each array. True positions retain source order and values/nulls; false/null mask positions disappear. Array outputs retain datatype, not standalone field/schema metadata.
cases.implementation_sketch:
let pred = FilterBuilder::new(&mask).optimize().build();
let out = arrays.iter().map(|a| pred.filter(a.as_ref())).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
cases.unknowns: No measured break-even count. Benchmark setup plus 20 applications across representative sizes, densities and types; check equality first.

cases.decision: Choose direct filter for this single small primitive array.
cases.decisive_conditions: One application offers no repeated-preparation amortization; optimized preparation consumes time and may increase memory.
cases.contract: Input: primitive array and same-domain BooleanArray. Output: fallible ArrayRef of the same value datatype, true positions only, in source order. False/null mask positions are excluded; selected input nulls remain. Kernels do not carry field/schema metadata. Reuse is semantically equivalent when the same mask is applied.
cases.implementation_sketch: let out = filter(&values, &mask)?;
cases.unknowns: Direct filtering is a workload-based choice, not a measured universal speed guarantee. If reuse/size changes, benchmark total builder setup and application against direct filtering.

cases.decision: Use take_record_batch after validating the known indices [2,0].
cases.decisive_conditions: Two columns provide an unambiguous output row count; both indices are non-null and less than three.
cases.contract: The helper gathers each column and reconstructs with try_new. Output has two rows in order [row2,row0], original column order/types/schema, and preserved value nulls. Construction requires nonempty columns, schema/column count and datatype agreement, equal column lengths, and valid top-level nullability. The helper uses unchecked array take; untrusted indices require prevalidation or checked per-column take.
cases.unknowns: Sketch assertions were not executed; nested schema behavior is not exhaustively qualified.

cases.decision: Validate indices, then construct the empty-column output with row_count=2 explicitly.
cases.decisive_conditions: Zero columns cannot supply a length. This pin's take_record_batch reconstructs with try_new and errors for an empty column vector.
cases.contract: The input must itself represent three rows via explicit row_count. Validate every non-null index against input.num_rows(), even though there are no value buffers to access. Preserve the empty schema and its metadata. Output has zero columns and two rows; row order is unobservable without values but multiplicity remains in row_count. try_new_with_options returns Result.
cases.unknowns: No new execution performed; the helper limitation is supported by the brief and retained named receipt.

cases.decision: Use cast_with_options with safe=true.
cases.decisive_conditions: Continue through malformed values for the supported Utf8-to-Int32 conversion.
cases.contract: Input strings ["12","bad",null] produce Int32 [12,null,null], preserving length and position. The return is Result<ArrayRef, ArrowError>; safe=true is null-on-value-failure, not assurance every type pair succeeds. Unsupported casts may error. Output field must permit nulls; arrays do not preserve field/schema metadata. Failed parses and input nulls become indistinguishable unless separately recorded.
cases.implementation_sketch:
let opts = CastOptions { safe: true, ..Default::default() };
let out = cast_with_options(&strings, &DataType::Int32, &opts)?;
cases.unknowns: This specific conversion is covered by retained reference evidence; no new run. Other precision/overflow/type-pair rules require separate checks.

cases.decision: Use cast_with_options with safe=false.
cases.decisive_conditions: Malformed non-null strings must reject the conversion.
cases.contract: For ["12","bad",null] to Int32, "bad" causes Err rather than a successful partially converted array. Valid strings convert and input nulls remain null when conversion otherwise succeeds. The type-pair predicate can_cast_types does not certify all values. Preserve schema metadata explicitly if rebuilding a batch and allow genuine input nulls.
cases.unknowns: Exact error text is not established here. Sketch assertions are proposed; retained receipt supplies only prior reference evidence.

cases.decision: Use RowConverter for repeated local composite comparisons; use lexsort_to_indices if only sorted positions are needed.
cases.decisive_conditions: Specify direction and null placement separately per field; compare only rows produced by the same converter.
cases.contract: Ordered ArrayRef columns become Rows. Borrowed Row views depend on Rows; owned() detaches one row into OwnedRow. Mixed sort policies are encoded per column. convert_columns may panic on a schema mismatch; construction/conversion otherwise expose Results. convert_rows yields arrays, not a schema, and panics for foreign-converter rows. Row bytes are not stable serialization.
cases.unknowns: Application collation/canonical equality and full nested/float semantics need explicit policy.

cases.decision: Persist typed key columns and schema in Arrow IPC, with an explicit application version/sort-policy manifest. Rebuild comparison rows after reading.
cases.decisive_conditions: Cross-process and upgrade durability excludes treating RowConverter bytes as an unspecified permanent key encoding.
cases.contract: Write RecordBatches, finish the footer, then read batches/schema. Logical values, nulls and types are the interchange payload; comparison direction/null placement must accompany them as explicit policy. Writer/reader operations are fallible; footer and endianness compatibility can reject a file. RowConverter remains local to each reader/converter lifecycle.
cases.unknowns: No cross-version roundtrip was executed; qualify the permitted IPC types/features and future readers. IPC does not itself define application canonical key identity.

cases.decision: Use RowConverter with the dictionary column datatype in its SortField; accept hydrated decoded strings.
cases.decisive_conditions: Only logical values matter, so losing dictionary keys/assignments is acceptable.
cases.contract: Dictionary<Int8,Utf8> inputs participate in comparisons through their string values, not key numbers. convert_rows returns Utf8 arrays rather than Dictionary<Int8,Utf8>. Other string value datatypes must be checked explicitly. Preserve null/value/order semantics, but reconstruct output schema from decoded datatypes rather than blindly reusing dictionary fields. Rows must originate from the same converter; foreign rows/schema mismatches can panic.
cases.unknowns: Retained coverage is Int8/Utf8; other dictionary/string layouts are not runtime-qualified here.

cases.decision: Keep dictionary keys, ordered dictionary values, key datatype and schema separately while using RowConverter only for comparisons.
cases.decisive_conditions: RowConverter decoding alone cannot recover exact physical dictionaries or original assignments; value equality loses that information.
cases.contract: For Dictionary<Int8,Utf8>, row decoding yields Utf8. Exact reconstruction instead uses preserved Int8 keys plus the original Utf8 dictionary, producing Dictionary<Int8,Utf8>. Retain unused/duplicate dictionary entries and key validity. Reordering requires gathering original keys by row identity, then reusing the original dictionary. try_new rejects out-of-range/negative valid keys; preserve field metadata separately.
cases.implementation_sketch:
let restored = DictionaryArray::<Int8Type>::try_new(original_keys.clone(), original_values.clone())?;
// If reordered, checked-take the keys in comparison-result order first.
cases.unknowns: No executed exact-dictionary roundtrip exists here. Persisting this side representation needs its own explicit format contract; do not infer it from logical string roundtrip.

cases.decision: Use execute_stream and await consumption of each batch; use partitioned streams only with bounded caller concurrency.
cases.decisive_conditions: Incremental result handling is required, without intentionally retaining all outputs.
cases.contract: Terminal APIs consume DataFrame. Stream creation and subsequent polling can fail independently. execute_stream returns SendableRecordBatchStream; collect buffers Vec<RecordBatch>. Streaming avoids terminal full-result retention but does not bound operators, prefetch, caches, consumer buffers or process RSS. Batch schemas follow the plan; one stream does not imply global sorting. Dropping the stream aborts its query execution; retained batches remain owned by the caller.
cases.unknowns: No memory/RSS or cancellation-latency guarantee was measured; backpressure depends on consumer retention and concurrency.

cases.decision: Stream outputs, configure a shared budgeted RuntimeEnv and usable spill storage, and qualify the blocking sort under load.
cases.decisive_conditions: The sort can retain substantial state before producing output; streaming alone cannot satisfy the budget.
cases.contract: Set memory_limit, spill mode/directory/capacity, sort reservation, batch size and concurrency. with_memory_limit budgets participating allocations, explicitly not all allocations/RSS. Sort may spill or return a resource error. Share RuntimeEnv across contexts when the budget is process-wide. Handle creation/poll errors; ORDER BY semantics come from the plan.
cases.unknowns: Require physical-plan/metrics inspection, representative cardinality/concurrency, spill and failure controls, and measured peak RSS. A hard RSS ceiling needs external enforcement. Retained 1-byte failure evidence establishes no production bound.

cases.decision: Register a MemTable; no custom provider is needed for already materialized partitioned batches.
cases.decisive_conditions: The input is Vec<Vec<RecordBatch>>, with outer vectors representing partitions; at least one partition is required.
cases.contract: Provide a compatible SchemaRef and batches; construction/registration are fallible. An empty table uses vec![vec![]]. Values, nulls and duplicates remain relational data; partitioning does not establish global output order. Batches stay resident for table reuse. ViewTable reuses a logical plan, not necessarily results. Custom TableProvider is justified only by behavior these providers cannot express.
cases.unknowns: Consumer features and batch-schema compatibility still require validation. This design evaluation did not execute registration or queries.

cases.decision: Use ListingTable with ParquetFormat and object-store registration; retain built-in partition/statistics pruning.
cases.decisive_conditions: Files and metadata, rather than resident batches, are the source. Custom providers are reserved for additional source semantics.
cases.contract: Map the URL prefix to an authenticated ObjectStore. Configure .parquet discovery, typed path partition columns and file-only schema; with_schema excludes partition columns. Nonconforming partition paths may be ignored. Enable row-group statistics pruning. Plan/execution can fail on schema, store or read errors. SQL nulls/duplicates survive; no global ordering is implied.
cases.unknowns: Inspect pruning metrics and compare results with an unpruned fixture. Cloud authentication, listing costs and bytes read are unverified.

cases.decision: Classify each fully supported predicate Exact; unsupported expressions remain Unsupported.
cases.decisive_conditions: Every candidate row is evaluated under the same SQL typing/null semantics, with no false positives or false negatives.
cases.contract: Return one classification per input expression in matching order. Accepted filters are conjunctive; only TRUE rows survive, preserving duplicates. Exact lets DataFusion remove residual filtering. Scan returns an ExecutionPlan with requested schema/projection; evaluating all rows alone does not establish semantic correctness.
cases.implementation_sketch:
Ok(filters.iter().map(|e| if fully_supported(e) { Exact } else { Unsupported }).collect())
// fully_supported is an application capability check, not an upstream API.
cases.unknowns: The Exact variant rustdoc says "omit ... tuples which pass", contradicting scan docs. The decision follows the fuller scan contract and brief.
cases.correctness_oracle: Compare result multisets against Unsupported/reference execution using b>1 over [0,null,2,2,3]: [2,2,3]. Inspect absence of residual only for supported Exact expressions; add boundary/type controls.

cases.decision: Classify conservative metadata group pruning Inexact.
cases.decisive_conditions: Groups may contain false positives, but pruning must retain every row satisfying the SQL predicate.
cases.contract: Return classifications in input order. DataFusion keeps a residual Filter to remove candidates that fail or evaluate NULL. Never push a raw candidate limit below that residual; too few qualifying rows could remain. Missing/uncertain statistics must keep groups. Unknown predicates are Unsupported. Return the requested scan schema without deduplicating candidates.
cases.implementation_sketch:
Ok(filters.iter().map(|e| if sound_metadata_pruning(e) { Inexact } else { Unsupported }).collect())
// Helper denotes the provider's reviewed capability test.
cases.unknowns: The retained probe uses an all-candidate Inexact provider; it does not qualify a min/max implementation.
cases.correctness_oracle: Compare final bags to unpruned execution, including [0,null,2,2,3], mixed groups, missing stats and boundary matches. Assert every reference row survives candidate generation; inspect residual filtering and absence of unsafe pushed limits.

cases.decision: For accepted Exact predicates, evaluate the conjunction before returning all columns.
cases.decisive_conditions: projection=None requires the provider's full schema; capability checks must cover each predicate's actual types/operators.
cases.contract: Input: Session, projection, filters, limit. Output: Arc<dyn ExecutionPlan>, later yielding fallible batches. Keep predicate columns available. Boolean TRUE qualifies; false/NULL do not. Preserve duplicate rows, datatype/nullability/metadata and column order. If a limit exists, count qualifying rows, not candidates; returning more is permitted. Do not promise an ordering the physical source lacks.
cases.unknowns: Production source execution and predicate evaluator equivalence remain unverified.
cases.correctness_oracle: Differentially compare all-column bags and schemas with Unsupported/reference scans over nulls, duplicate matches, nonmatches and all-null predicates; do not compare sets.

cases.decision: Evaluate predicates using internal required columns, apply a qualifying-row limit, then project.
cases.decisive_conditions: The predicate column may be absent from requested output. A small pushed limit is safe only after exact filtering.
cases.contract: Return projected fields in requested index order, with corresponding types/nullability/metadata. Count qualifying rows across batches/partitions; produce at least limit matches when available, possibly more, and all available matches if fewer. SQL NULL predicates do not qualify; duplicates remain. Never project away the predicate input or stop after limit raw candidates. Inexact filtering requires residual evaluation without that pushed limit.
cases.unknowns: The sketch is a batch step, not a complete partition-coordinated ExecutionPlan.
cases.correctness_oracle: Use leading nonmatches/nulls then duplicate matches; compare projected schema and qualifying bags to reference, verify count min(limit,total_matches), and use explicit ordering for deterministic limited-query comparison.

cases.decision: Enter ordinary SQL planning and let session analysis supply supported coercions before optimization/evaluation.
cases.decisive_conditions: Mixed operand types are resolvable only if the operator/function has a supported common-type rule.
cases.contract: Constructing Expr/UDF calls does not itself evaluate or guarantee compatibility. Analyzer coercion inserts casts; simplification folds constants/algebraic forms; physical planning creates typed executable expressions; execution yields values. Unsupported combinations can fail during planning or evaluation. Inspect output field/type/nullability; ordinary addition propagates NULL. create_physical_expr applies coercion/rewrites but does not itself simplify.
cases.implementation_sketch:
let df = ctx.sql("SELECT CAST(1 AS INT) + CAST(2 AS BIGINT) AS n").await?;
let stream = df.execute_stream().await?;
cases.unknowns: Expected integer result is 3, but the exact inferred field and arbitrary mixed-type rules need inspection; no execution occurred.

cases.decision: Explicitly coerce against the intended DFSchema before calling simplify outside normal analysis.
cases.decisive_conditions: Construction can produce incompatible operands; simplification assumes types appropriate for the operator.
cases.contract: coerce returns Result<Expr>; no supported common type means rejection or another explicit policy, not arbitrary implicit success. simplify may error or leave an uncoerced expression unchanged, so Ok does not prove compatibility. Use a typed schema/context, then physical planning and evaluation; ColumnarValue may be scalar or array. Validate output type, nullability, value and batch length.
cases.unknowns: An unsupported pair may fail at different stages. The retained mixed-integer example is not a complete coercion matrix.

cases.decision: Express selected/skipped ranges in the concatenated rows of all retained groups; with all groups retained this is the file row domain.
cases.decisive_conditions: Known row positions select ranges; RowSelection does not implement arbitrary ordered gathers/duplicates.
cases.contract: For three 3-row groups, original row7 is selected-domain position7: skip7/select1/skip1. Selection applies before RowFilter. RowFilter decodes predicate columns before final projected output; row-group statistics pruning excludes entire groups earlier. RowSelection can avoid page fetching/decoding, especially with page indexes, but result equality proves no I/O saving. Builder/read operations are fallible; validate group/range bounds.
cases.implementation_sketch:
let sel: RowSelection = vec![RowSelector::skip(7), RowSelector::select(1), RowSelector::skip(1)].into();
let reader = builder.with_row_selection(sel).build()?;
cases.unknowns: Preserve/test selected row identity, values/nulls and projected schema against an unselected reader; measure bytes and decode work separately.

cases.decision: Choose retained row groups first, then rebase selection offsets over their concatenated rows.
cases.decisive_conditions: Excluded groups contribute zero rows to RowSelection coordinates.
cases.contract: For three 3-row groups retaining [0,2], original row7 becomes position4: skip4/select1/skip1 over six retained rows. Reusing file-wide skip7 is wrong. Group selection precedes RowSelection, which precedes decode-time RowFilter and final projection. Metadata pruning excludes candidate storage units; RowFilter requires decoded values. RowSelection may skip page I/O, but output equality does not measure source savings. Validate group bounds, selection span, output identities/nulls/schema and fallible reads.
cases.implementation_sketch:
let sel: RowSelection = vec![RowSelector::skip(4), RowSelector::select(1), RowSelector::skip(1)].into();
let reader = builder.with_row_groups(vec![0, 2]).with_row_selection(sel).build()?;
cases.unknowns: Retained evidence tests coordinates, not cloud I/O/page bytes. Compare with an unpruned reader using original row identities.
